correctness.rationale: The state set is exactly the 2,000 nine-edge trees of KG(5,2), independently obtained from exhaustive DSU filtering of 5,005 sets and from the integer matrix-tree determinant. The fundamental-cycle lemma proves there are exactly two allowed incident-edge pivots per omitted edge. A delivered, reproducibly executed standard-library checker generates identical adjacency lists by exchange filtering and fundamental-path pivots; all 2,000 full breadth-first searches prove the diameter and exact distance/excess tables. An independent 21-orbit-weighted BFS on the second adjacency representation agrees on each histogram and eccentricity, and the full 120-permutation action certifies the two extreme-pair orbits. These are finite exhaustive proofs, not extrapolations.

value.rationale: The archive-era locally constrained Gray-code problem motivates exact pivot distances, which cannot be inferred from ordinary graphic-matroid basis exchanges. Petersen is the canonical ten-vertex nonplanar cubic graph; its natural 2,000-tree pivot graph has diameter 8 rather than the unrestricted exchange bound 6. The complete metric table, localized maximal four-move detour, and exact two-orbit decomposition of the 150 extremal pairs give a natural, reusable reconfiguration benchmark, not a routine tree count or arbitrary slice.
